messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Change the person's identity to match the person in the reference photo. Use the reference photo only to determine the target person's facial identity and skin tone. Apply that skin tone consistently to the face and body. Retain the current hairstyle, hair color, clothing, expression, action, scene, and camera.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Only compare editing requirements; historical appearance words are not observed facts.","original_user_request":"Using the provided source video, apply the following edit: Please change the person's identity to match the person in the reference photo. Only use the reference photo to determine the target person's facial identity and skin tone. Apply that skin tone consistently to the face and body, while retaining the current hairstyle, hair color, clothing, expression, action, scene, and camera.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The woman stands facing forward, then turns her body and head to the side while raising her hand to touch her hair, before turning back to face the camera.","camera":"A static, medium-full shot from a slightly low angle, keeping the subject centered in the frame.","clothing":"A white off-the-shoulder top with puffy sleeves, a pink and white gingham corset-style midsection, and a two-toned black and white skirt, paired with light blue sneakers.","hair_color":"Red","hairstyle":"Short, spiky red hair that appears to move or shift during the sequence.","identity":"A 3D-rendered woman with a slim build, dark skin, and a neutral facial expression.","scene":"An outdoor amusement park setting at dusk, featuring a large Ferris wheel, a ticket booth with a red roof, and a paved ground area."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The output remains visually almost identical to the source: same red spiky hair, same outfit, same amusement park scene, same camera framing, and the same dark-skinned woman performing the same motion. No clear facial identity change toward the reference person is visible.
arguments.requested_change: Change the person's facial identity and skin tone to match the reference photo, applying the skin tone consistently to face and body while retaining hairstyle, hair color, clothing, expression, action, scene, and camera.
uncertain: Whether subtle facial identity changes occurred is difficult to judge from the provided frames, but no visible change toward the reference identity is apparent.
